reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it presents a step-by-step guide to Binance signup, referral checking, identity verification, and spot and futures trading. Referral incentives are described with some eligibility conditions, but the available video evidence gives no indication that they are deceptive or lead to a harmful destination. The leverage warning and security guidance fit the exchange onboarding and trading context.

citations.quote: Binance Beginner Guide From Sign Up to First Trade Step by Step
If you register through this link, the referral code will be automatically applied.
First, when signing up it is highly recommended to apply a referral. This is because you receive a 20% trading fee discount.
Then upload photos of the front and back of your ID card. After uploading, you will proceed to real-time Facial Verification.
With market order enter the quantity and press buy and trade will be executed immediately.

opening.argument: Judge, the offer is tied to specific actions, not merely mentioned in passing. The description promises a fee discount, a bonus and payback, then directs viewers to register through its link to apply the referral code. It also pairs a deposit with an additional bonus. The tutorial gives viewers a route from account creation to trading, but the reward-for-action sequence deserves scrutiny as a financial solicitation: the viewer is encouraged to sign up through the supplied link and deposit funds on the strength of advertised benefits.

Deposit 10 USDT and receive an additional 10 USDT bonus!

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense's account of signup and trading steps does not address the deposit-for-bonus offer. Nor does a statement that a referral code is automatically applied establish when the advertised bonus or payback becomes available. Teaching the mechanics of an exchange and soliciting a rewarded signup can occur in the same video; the former does not settle how the latter should be judged.

citations.quote: If you register through this link, the referral code will be automatically applied.
Deposit 10 USDT and receive an additional 10 USDT bonus!

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The quoted offers establish a referral promotion, not a deceptive payout or harmful destination. The description states eligibility conditions for existing users, and the video continues through identity verification and actual order mechanics. A deposit-linked bonus alone does not establish that funds are being misdirected or that a promised reward is unavailable.

With market order enter the quantity and press buy and trade will be executed immediately.

opening.argument: Judge, consider the signals together. The description leads with a discount, a $600 bonus and $50 payback beside a link; it separately offers an additional bonus for depositing USDT. The narration tells viewers that foregoing the referral could be a loss. It then walks them through uploading both sides of an ID and completing facial verification. That combination of reward pressure, an external signup link, a requested deposit and sensitive-data submission warrants more concern than the beginner-guide title suggests, even without proof of what happens after a viewer follows the link.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: These are reasons to examine the offer, not evidence that the video deceives viewers. opening.argument: Judge, the tutorial format also serves a promotional path. Before explaining signup, the narrator recommends applying a referral, calls missing it a loss and directs viewers to the link he provided. The description says registration through that link applies the code automatically, while the signup screen displays rewards beside the account-creation controls. These details make the referral more than incidental background: the lesson steers a beginner toward a particular signup route by foregrounding financial benefits. Its instructional sections should not obscure that solicitation.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense lists genuine instructional topics, but that does not make the referral peripheral. The narrator opens by explaining how to check that his linked referral was applied, before returning to signup. The question is not whether the video teaches trading; it is whether that teaching also moves viewers toward the promoted, reward-linked registration.

citations.quote: show you how to check whether the Binance referral 20% Trading Fee discount was properly applied.
Now let's return to the main topic and start with the sign-up process.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A referral can be promotional without being a scam. The narrator explicitly returns to the main signup process, and the video goes on to explain identity verification, spot orders and futures risk. The cited referral material shows a disclosed incentive and a preferred registration route; it does not show deception or displace the operational guide as the video's main subject.
